session.result:
The native expression evaluator now hands node-reference results to the engine when they aren't shaped like items. The tests, typecheck and lint pass, but I couldn't show the actual divergence from the engine this guards against. Legacy and quickjs already return the same results either way, and the `vm` engine, which is where I'd expect the difference, doesn't run in this environment.

**Cause.** The native evaluator assumed that `$('X').item`, `$input.item`, `first()`, `last()` and `all()` always return items (`{ json, ... }`) or, for `all()`, a list of them. It never checked. The data proxy can return other things:
- In `combined` binary mode it returns the item's `json` in place of the item (`returnExecutionData` in `src/workflow-data-proxy.ts:139`).
- `first()` and `last()` return `undefined` when there are no items.

These values went straight into native member reads instead of being left to the engine.

**Change** (in `src/expressions/native-evaluation/evaluator.ts`):
- I added an `isItem` check: the value is a plain object with its own `json` property, and that property is a plain object too.
- `evalNodeRefCall` now requires `first()`/`last()` to return an item and `all()` to return an array of items. Otherwise it hands the expression to the engine.
- `evalMember` applies the same check to `.item` on `$(...)` and `$input`. Legacy `$node[...]` reads are not checked, because their `.json`/`.binary` are the item's own fields, not items.
- An empty `all()` result (`[]`) is still evaluated natively.

**Tests** (in `test/native-evaluation-parity.test.ts`):
- A new unit test covers both outcomes. Item-shaped results are evaluated natively. Non-items, `undefined`, and mixed `all()` arrays go to the engine.
- New parity cases run against a workflow set to `binaryMode: 'combined'` and check that native evaluation and the engine return the same result.
- I updated the existing per-item charging test: its `$input.all()` stub returned numbers, so it now returns `{ json: {} }` items.

**Verification:**
- The parity, fuzz, corpus-coverage, data-proxy and expression test files all pass on the legacy and quickjs engines (9 files). Every expression in the handled corpus is still evaluated natively.
- With the check turned off, only the new unit test fails. The combined-mode parity cases pass either way on these two engines, so they guard against regressions but don't reproduce a bug here.
- `acdc-typecheck` printed no errors (I couldn't read its exit code) and `acdc-lint` is clean.

evidence:
## fix(core): Hand node reference results without an item shape to the engine (no-changelog)

Native expression evaluation assumed node reference results (`.item`, `first()`, `last()`, `all()` on `$()`/`$input`) are always items, but the data proxy can return the item's json in place of the item (combined binary mode) or undefined (no items). Added an `isItem` check (own plain-object `json`) in evaluator.ts: evalNodeRefCall checks first/last results and every all() element, and evalMember checks `.item` on non-legacy node refs, falling back to the engine (EngineFallbackError) otherwise. Updated the existing all()-charging test to use item-shaped stubs; added a unit test for the fallback and combined-binary-mode parity cases.

### What changed
- 1 source file(s), 1 test file(s), 116 changed lines
- `packages/workflow/src/expressions/native-evaluation/evaluator.ts`

### What ran
- The agent ran the tests 4 time(s) and says: acdc-test on native-evaluation-parity, native-evaluation-fuzz, native-evaluation-corpus-coverage, workflow-data-proxy and expression tests: 9 files passed (legacy and quickjs projects; the vm project did not run here). With the check turned off, only the new unit test fails; the combined-mode parity cases pass either way on legacy/quickjs. acdc-typecheck printed no errors (exit code not observed); acdc-lint on both changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Type check: passes; lint: passes
- Tests for the issue: 0/1; tests that passed before: 458/459
- **The agent said the tests pass; the tests for the issue do not.**

### Risks that remain
- Change risk: medium (17% chance of a revert or follow-up fix, from n8n's history)
- Not reproduced: no engine run here diverged from native for non-item results (legacy/quickjs pass either way); the motivating divergence is presumably in the vm bridge, whose source and test project were not available here
- In combined binary mode, a json that happens to have an own object-valued `json` key still passes as item-shaped and stays native
- first()/last() returning undefined now goes to the engine instead of being evaluated natively — slower, but the result should be the same
- all() now runs an O(n) shape check over at most MAX_RESULT_LENGTH elements on each call, including inside callback bodies

### Where a person decides
- Autonomy level: **agent reviewed**
- category bugfix: at most agent_reviewed

- Agent cost: $1.03

judge.reason: The change makes node reference calls fall back to the engine unless they return a real item (or an array of items), which covers the issue. It is stricter than the merged fix: it requires an object `json` and also falls back on `undefined`. The hidden tests probably fail on that, since the merged fix keeps `undefined` and any non-array object native. Output stays correct either way. The cost is only some lost native-path performance, plus a somewhat wider scope with the extra `.item` guard in `evalMember`.
